rationale: This is a simple linear combination of two long-published anomalies (Sloan accruals and Titman-Wei-Xie capital investment) that are both documented to predict returns *negatively*, so differencing them implicitly bets the capex leg has the opposite of its established sign without any argument for why.

The multiplicative weighting is internally inconsistent for the large fraction of firms with negative asset growth, where a *high* accrual rank makes the signal more negative and thus predicts *higher* returns — the exact opposite of the stated conditional mechanism — and the underlying asset-growth/accrual overlap is already well documented.

The bounded accrual-versus-capex composition share is a genuinely scale-neutral construction that is not a standard published variable, though it will be numerically unstable and effectively noise-dominated for asset-light, near-zero-capex firms and risks collapsing into a monotone re-expression of plain accruals.

Both legs are components of the Richardson-Sloan-Soliman-Tuna balance-sheet accrual decomposition and both ΔWC and ΔPPE are documented to predict returns negatively, so subtracting the PPE leg contradicts the published sign and leaves the signal essentially a rediscovery of working-capital accruals.
(oancf − capx)/at is simply free cash flow to assets, a standard textbook variable and known return predictor, so this is a rediscovery rather than a cross-theme interaction.

The three-year acquisition-intensity plus accrual-intensity rank stack is coherent, sign-consistent across both legs, and adds persistence, but it is an equal-weight index of two already-known anomalies rather than the "novel" interaction claimed, and the COALESCE(aqc,0) will create a large tie mass that concentrates the ranking in the accrual leg.
